A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAC-Opt and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.9. Despite the changed title, the complete 19-page versions support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAC-Opt accuracy, runtime, ablation, verification, and case-study results, including convergence and extraction analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations across seven datasets and reports revised accuracy and runtime values in several main-text and appendix tables.

M1.justification: The extraction, translation, reconstruction, semantic verification, selective correction, and debugging procedures remain unchanged. Added component notation in Section 3.5 restates the existing model assembly.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NL4OPT, IndustryOR, EasyLP, ComplexLP, NLP4LP, ReSocratic, and ComplexOR. The cutting-stock and flowshop-scheduling case studies and appendix extraction audit are also retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Standard, CoT, CoE, CAFA, Reflexion, OptiMUS-0.2, and OptiMUS-0.3. Table 5 corrects a summary value to CoE's already reported ComplexOR score without introducing a new evaluated method.

E3.justification: The reported datasets, sample counts, accuracy criterion, shared extraction pipeline, and model configurations are unchanged. Both versions retain three debugging attempts, five correction iterations, and a similarity threshold of 0.75; the numerical revisions do not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The correction/debugging ablations, Qwen generalization evaluation, verifier comparison, case studies, extraction audit, and correction-count analysis are retained. Some existing scores change, but no analysis question, ablation condition, or case-study evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over five independent runs and retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Table 4 and Figure 3. No additional runs, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests are documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 revise several IndustryOR and ComplexOR accuracies, including SAC-Opt's IndustryOR score from 63.7% to 63.8% and OptiMUS-0.3's from 54.0% to 54.3%. SAC-Opt's IndustryOR runtime changes from 79.00 to 80.20 seconds in Tables 4, 5, and 7. Table 5 changes the ComplexOR best-baseline accuracy from 52.2% to 57.1%, matching CoE in Table 1. Ablation values and summary gains receive small updates; the main rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12, Algorithm 1, and the appendix convergence discussion are unchanged. Section 3.5 merely adds previously defined symbols beside the model components; no mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion revise the headline average accuracy gain from 7.8% to 7.7%. The first-contribution novelty statement shifts from semantics-driven correction to proactive semantic verification that detects silent errors. The seven-dataset scope and 21.9% ComplexLP gain remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 is rewritten but retains the interpretation that gains arise from semantic correction across sufficiently capable LLMs. The extraction dependence discussed in Appendix A.6 and the runtime and verification-cost limitations in Appendix A.8 are unchanged.

D1.justification: The Python/Gurobi implementation, shared OptiMUS-0.3 extraction strategy, SentenceTransformer configuration, appendix prompts and structured-data example, and source-code access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes Pyomo and its Hart et al. (2011) citation from the introduction and bibliography. Novelty positioning now emphasizes proactive semantic verification; the related-work sections otherwise retain the same literature and relationships.

P1.justification: The title now explicitly names SAC-Opt and iterative correction. The contribution list and Section 4.6 receive localized rewrites, with a small explanatory notation addition in Section 3.5. Section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Title and prose edits cause limited local reflow, and the shortened bibliography moves the Yang et al. reference from page 12 to page 11. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–7 retain their designs, captions, and placement; numerical table revisions do not constitute display redesigns.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves presentation and internal consistency. Table 5's corrected ComplexOR baseline now agrees with Table 1 and its reported 1.8-point gain, while the title identifies the method and correction mechanism more clearly. The benefit is limited: updating the headline gain to 7.7% leaves an introduction sentence at 7.8%, and Table 5 still contains inconsistent EasyLP and ComplexLP best-baseline values.
